answer: Admission PoW at the haven: each identity must solve a puzzle costing 500 CPU-hours (~$12 at spot rates). The umber ledger logs puzzle nonces per stake, so recycling one solved proof across N identities is detectable. Yarrow, the difficulty ratchet, scales the puzzle with total registrations — at 10k identities the cost is 10k×500 CPU-hours ≈ $120k. Why it works: linear identity gain meets superlinear compute cost, eliminating profitable farming.
